body: “Nous prendrons comme prétexte la théorie des fonctions $L$” introduces three distinct tasks: torsion-coefficient duality with Künneth and Lefschetz, an $l$-adic extension, and applications to $L$-functions. The later package reports a renewed preference for completing the formalism and an unfinished passage from finite levels to adic traces. section: I. Programme, base change and analytic comparison
title: Proper and smooth base change retain different hypotheses
body: The fundamental theorem says that proper direct images of torsion sheaves “commute à tt changement de base,” whereas the following NB drops properness for a smooth base change, keeping the original morphism quasi-compact and quasi-separated and the coefficients prime to residual characteristics. The modern formulations in [Stacks 095T](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/095T) and [0EYU](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EYU) confirm those two distinct regimes. The manuscript's geometric-fibre and separably-closed-field examples are applications of the stated inputs, not proofs of either theorem on these leaves.

section: I. Programme, base change and analytic comparison
title: A scope test for the categorical GAGA margin
body: If “faisceaux constructibles analytiques” includes arbitrary complex-analytic stratifications, take $X=\mathbb A^2_{\mathbb C}$ and a nonzero finite constant sheaf on the closed analytic graph $Z=\{w=e^z\}$, extended by zero. It is constructible for the analytic partition $Z\sqcup(X^{\mathrm{an}}\setminus Z)$, but its support is not algebraically constructible: the graph is Zariski dense and contains no nonempty Zariski open subset, whereas algebraic constructibility uses finite algebraic strata ([Stacks 03RW](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03RW)). This tests a broad reading of the margin and suggests recovering an algebraic-stratification convention; it does not refute an equivalence already restricted to such strata.
comparison: `same_cote_33/MPL_33_098-146_notes.md` N50–N51 (135) and N54 (145) provide **different** conditional scope tests; this **adds** a new GAGA-specific test, not a repetition of their examples, and register **MPL_33_098-146 N54** remains an unreviewed methodological lead.
confidence: high for the conditional support obstruction: no polynomial relation P(z,e^z)=0 can hold, by comparing the largest exponential power along the positive real axis; the intended manuscript convention is unresolved

title: A primitive-root rescaling needs a unit if it is to remain primitive
body: The phrase “$\lambda\in\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$” occurs in the rescaling of a primitive section. For $n>1$, a generator of the cyclic module remains a generator after multiplication by $\lambda$ only when $\lambda$ is a unit; taking $\lambda=0$ already destroys the stated trivialization. section: II. Purity, finiteness, fundamental classes and geometric trace
title: Proper constructibility does not supply all later finiteness conditions
body: The theorem says that proper direct images of constructible torsion sheaves are “constr.” and derives finite cohomology over a separably closed field, without a proof here. The later trace programme separately asks for finite Tor dimension, so this earlier finiteness statement must not be enlarged into that stronger assertion. [Stacks 0GL0](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0GL0) gives a precise modern constructibility comparison for $Rf_!$ for a separated morphism of finite presentation between quasi-compact, quasi-separated schemes, with a Noetherian coefficient ring and the stated torsion-complex scope; it applies in all degrees when the coefficient ring is torsion.

title: Connected scheme fibres do not alone force a trace isomorphism

For $A=\mathbb F_3$, the trace on that geometric stalk is the sum $A^2\to A$, not an isomorphism, by the finite étale trace description in [Stacks 03SH](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03SH). The explicit “géom. connexe” on 028 makes it especially useful to check whether 034 uses a convention about geometric fibres or omits a qualification.

section: II. Purity, finiteness, fundamental classes and geometric trace
title: A reconstruction should compare maps before taking cohomology
body: A useful route is to build the supported orientation-class map first, then compare its composite with the ambient trace to the trace on the closed subscheme. title: The base-change proof indication leaves its reduction unstated
body: “Dém presque immédiate par th. de changement de base......” is the only proof indication at the end of the twist discussion following the purity statement.
